title: DOOM
summary: Genre-defining first-person shooter featuring 3D graphics engine, networked deathmatch multiplayer, moddable WAD files, and intense demon-slaying action.
facts: Designed by John Carmack, John Romero, Adrian Carmack, and Tom Hall.
Distributed as shareware episode 'Knee-Deep in the Dead', installed on millions of PCs worldwide.
Popularized multiplayer LAN deathmatching and custom WAD modding culture.

title: Half-Life
summary: Revolutionary sci-fi FPS game following physicist Gordon Freeman at Black Mesa, integrating seamless narrative storytelling without cutscenes.
facts: Built on GoldSrc engine, a heavily modified version of the Quake engine.
Won over 50 Game of the Year awards in 1998.
Spawned legendary community mods including Counter-Strike, Day of Defeat, and Team Fortress Classic.

title: StarCraft
summary: Masterpiece real-time strategy (RTS) game featuring three asymmetric factions (Terran, Zerg, Protoss) and competitive Battle.net multiplayer.
facts: Became a cultural phenomenon and national esport in South Korea.
Expanded with StarCraft: Brood War in late 1998.

title: Quake
summary: Pioneering true 3D FPS game with full 3D polygonal rendering, dark gothic industrial soundtrack by Trent Reznor (Nine Inch Nails), and Client-Side Prediction networking.
facts: Engine designed by John Carmack supporting hardware 3D acceleration (GLQuake).
QuakeWorld update in 1996 enabled low-latency online multiplayer over dial-up internet.
Music and ambient sound design created by Trent Reznor.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
summary: Critically acclaimed 3D action-adventure title for Nintendo 64 that defined 3D target lock-on combat (Z-targeting) and camera mechanics.
facts: Directed by Shigeru Miyamoto and team at Nintendo EAD.
Pioneered context-sensitive action buttons and Z-targeting lock-on targeting.
Remains one of the highest-rated video games of all time on Metacritic (99/100).
